newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaichi president, chairman to resign--Kyodo.
newsitem.headline: Yamaichi president, chairman to resign--Kyodo.

text.p: The president and chairman of Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd will soon resign their posts to take responsibility for the brokerage's alleged involvement in a high-profile payoff scandal, Kyodo news agency reported.

The Kyodo report late on Wednesday referring to company president Atsuo Miki and chairman Tsugio Yukihira quoted unnamed banking sources. A Yamaichi spokesman said on Thursday that the two had not expressed an intention to resign.
Thursday's Nihon Keizai Shimbun newspaper quoted Miki as saying he would consider carefully whether he should resign as president.
Kyodo said Yukihira also intended to resign from the chairmanship of the Japan Securities Dealers' Association (JSDA), an industry body comprising brokerages in Japan.
The Yamaichi spokesman said: "They have not said anything about resignation. It is not yet the time (for them) to say anything as an investigation is now under way."
Jiji news agency said officials of the prosecutors office raided the homes of top Yamaichi executives, including Miki and Yukihira, earlier on Thursday.
Prosecutors and officials of Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange and Surveillance Commission, raided 10 Yamaichi offices on Wednesday looking for evidence of alleged violations.

Prosecutors said on Wednesday they suspected Yamaichi paid 79 million yen to a "sokaiya" corporate racketeer. Government sources close to the investigation said Yamaichi had generally admitted that the payments had been made to racketeer Ryuichi Koike.
For weeks, Japanese media had reported on Yamaichi's possible involvement in illicit stock deals but the company had denied the reports.
"It is only recently that we found out about questionable deals," Miki said in an interview with the Nihon Keizai Shimbun.
Miki said he had not met Koike, the paper said.

Miki said the linking of Yamaichi to the scandal would adversely affect business in its corporate division but the brokerage would still be able to post an interim and full-year profit in the current business year to March 31, 1998.
Yamaichi posted a parent current profit of 1.22 billion yen last fiscal year, down 91.9 percent from a year earlier. It has not given a specific profit forecast for 1997/98.
